root_cause.text: The EIP93 driver unregistered all crypto algorithms regardless of whether they were supported by hardware (as indicated by the options register), causing a panic when trying to unregister algorithms that were never registered on platforms with limited hardware capabilities.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a hardware support check in `eip93_unregister_algs()` using the same `eip93_algo_is_supported()` helper used during registration, and updates the removal path to read the options register before unregistering. The CVE description explicitly states: "Currently, all algorithms are unregistered, even those not supported by HW. This results in panic on platforms that don't have all options implemented in silicon."

candidates.rationale: This line unregisters all algorithms regardless of which were actually registered, causing a panic when trying to unregister algorithms skipped during registration due to hardware limitations.
This function definition accepts a count parameter but does not check whether each algorithm was previously registered; it blindly unregisters up to 'i' algorithms.
The loop unconditionally iterates over all algorithms from 0 to i, including those that were never registered due to hardware support checks, leading to unregistration of unregistered algorithms.
This statement attempts to unregister a symmetric cipher algorithm that may not have been registered if the hardware did not support it, directly causing a panic.

This continue (part of the AES unsupported check) skips registration of an algorithm; when the remove path unregisters all algorithms, this skipped algorithm will cause a panic because it was never registered.
This continue (part of TDES unsupported check) similarly skips registration of an algorithm, ensuring it remains unregistered and leads to a panic during the global unregistration in the remove path.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call unregisters all algorithms (full array size) regardless of whether they were registered, causing a panic when an algorithm that was skipped due to hardware support is attempted to be unregistered.

This statement attempts to unregister a symmetric cipher algorithm that may not have been registered if the hardware did not support it, directly causing a panic when unregistring an algorithm that was never registered.

This continue statement (for AES unsupported check) skips registration of an algorithm when the hardware does not support AES; because the unregister path does not check, this skipped algorithm causes a panic when unregistered.
This continue statement (for TDES unsupported check) skips registration of an algorithm when the hardware does not support TDES; the skipped algorithm is later blindly unregistered, causing a panic.
